guarantees.claim: When key_length_i does not match any Key_* case (default), i_pad_256, i_pad_512, o_pad_256, o_pad_512 remain as all-zero as set by the initial defaults.
guarantees.cond: key_length_i not in {Key_128, Key_256, Key_384, Key_512, Key_1024}

guarantees.claim: When key_length_i == Key_1024, i_pad_256 and o_pad_256 are forced to all zeros; i_pad_512 and o_pad_512 are assigned as secret_key_i[1023:0] XORed with full-block pad constants (0x36/0x5c).

For Key_128, Key_256, Key_384, Key_512, the block computes i_pad_256, i_pad_512, o_pad_256, o_pad_512 by taking the top secret_key_i bits (from 1023 down to 1024−key_length), zero-padding to BlockSizeSHA256/BlockSizeSHA512, and XORing with 0x36 repeated (i_pad) or 0x5c repeated (o_pad).

assumptions.claim: BlockSizeSHA256 and BlockSizeSHA512 must respectively equal the actual SHA-256 and SHA-512 block sizes in bits (e.g., 512 and 1024).
assumptions.risk: Incorrect block size values produce wrong zero-padding lengths and corrupt the HMAC pad, resulting in invalid HMAC output.

assumptions.claim: secret_key_i must present the HMAC key left-justified in bits [1023:1024−key_length_i]; lower bits are don't-care.
assumptions.cond: when key_length_i is one of the defined Key_* values
assumptions.risk: Misaligned key bits will be incorporated into the pad, causing HMAC to use an incorrect key and break security.

assumptions.claim: External logic must not drive key_length_i to an illegal value; the RTL does not signal an error and will output zero pads.
assumptions.risk: Zero pads effectively use a null HMAC key, which may allow forgery if downstream logic does not detect the condition.

uncertain_points.claim: Key_1024 forces i_pad_256 and o_pad_256 to zero with the comment 'not allowed to be configured for SHA-2 256'. It is unclear if this is intended as a complete block; a zero pad results in a known HMAC key (all zero after XOR) for SHA-256, which could be exploited if SHA-256 operation is not disabled.
uncertain_points.cond: key_length_i == Key_1024 and SHA-256 mode active
uncertain_points.risk: HMAC‐SHA-256 computed with a zeroed key pad can be forged, breaking integrity/authentication.

uncertain_points.claim: The default case leaves all pad outputs at zero without asserting any error or kill flag, similar to the Key_1024 zeroing. A transient invalid key_length_i could silently enable HMAC with a null key.
uncertain_points.risk: Silent null-key HMAC computation, leading to a potential security bypass.

uncertain_points.claim: The logic depends on block size parameters matching the instantiated SHA engine and on external selection of key_length_i and key alignment. Verification must confirm these are consistent at the top level.
uncertain_points.risk: Mismatch would produce functionally incorrect or insecure HMAC pads without any local check.
